Hard review to write considering that I do enjoy this game, but I can't look past the problems. For one, there is a growing issue with functionality and stability. New DLC releases with a major update every 3 months or so. This is great, but doesn't work well for a 4X where quality of content is more important. This also really hurts the games long term performance because the new content always breaks stuff, and the custodian team responsible for fixing the issues isn't able to keep up. As of now, the late game requires that you are familiar with the console commands to fix things, only the prethoryn scourge end game crisis actually works (occasionally unbidden works too, but if you destroy their one big fleet then the thing breaks), the leader system is completely messed up, and more. On top of that, there is almost no variation in game play (democracy plays the same as an empire plays the same as a gestault plays the same as a megacorp plays the same as a dictator), with there being plenty of other issues with the combat, internal rp, rp immersion, diplomacy (or lack there of), restrictive war mechanics, and more. The game is still fun, but it could be waaaaay better if they stopped giving out these poor fast food DLC's, fixed the broken content, and/or had some clear vision for the game.

I've played a decent amount of strategy type games. This one had the WORST tutorial. Most of what I needed to learn required external searches on youtube. For a complicated game, you should NOT have a bad tutorial. I also found the combat to be absolutely nonsensical. The best and strongest fleet should win, right? WRONG, in this game it's some obscure metric of exhaustion which is completely counter-intuitive. You will not win if you have the stronger army which should basically be the case in every strategy type game. This to me was the most frustrating part, I understand theres a learning curve for certain aspects but this butt-backward combat was just beyond comprehension and for sure the worst part.I ended up resetting and starting a new save file after learning I was doing something significantly wrong a few times, no issue with that just felt like I wasted significant time. The game is very captivating though I did sink some decent time into it (the exploration part I found mesmerizing), the score is quite nice too...however due to the aforementioned problems , I will likely not be firing up this game again.TLDR: Bad tutorial for an overly complicated game, AWFUL combat/warfare in a game where all you want to do is dominate.Poopy Dumpy

Stelaris is already a great game, and will get even better over time.

In short, it allows you to create whatever space empire you can think of, within realistic parameters, and try to survive in a randomly generated galaxy filled with other young empires, ancient and advanced stagnating civilisations, primitive alien species that have not achieved spaceflight yet and other interesting creatures and events. Every game feels and plays different and interesting. If I have any complaints about this game, it is that the mid game can be a bit boring when the political situation and the big players in the galaxy are already established, and the only thing you can do is manage your empire and wait for the late game crisises to come, but that can easily be fixed with more events.The game is also very moddable and there is already a wide variety of mods on the Steam workshop.

Overall, I highly recomend Stellaris to all strategy or SF lovers.

Stellaris is a dream come true. You get to conquer the whole galaxy. But it's certainly not for everyone:

- steep learning curve, frustrating in the beginning
- some intransparent mechanics (fight system, I had to check wikis)
- performance/scaling issues (i4460+r9 290, drops to 20 fps with 6k+ fleets)
- bugs (have become much less, but still sometimes ruin a game)

If you can see past that:

- Lots of choices, e.g. for development and ethics
- Cool lore, rewarding quests
- SP and MP both great
- complex micromanagement

There was once a time when base game empires were mechanically differentiated from one another at a fundamental level from the very start of the game. Before the version 2.0 FTL rework, every empire had a meaningful choice that they had to make during empire creation: they had to choose if they wanted to use warp drives, jump drives, and hyper drives. These FTL methods fundamentally changed the way that fleets moved on the map and dictated the strategies for attacking and defending systems.

Now every single base game empire is exactly the same. The only changes you can make during empire creation are cosmetic or minor buffs and debuffs. Every war boils down to dogpiling a fortress placed on a strategic choke point with every fleet you can spare and watching a pair of HP bars grinding each other down until one hits zero. It does not arouse the imagination nor does it require any real thought or consideration for strategy or tactics. The soul of the game is dead.

To begin I've sunk over 1700 hours into this game and have been playing since release. I've picked up every DLC, played with and without mods, done some achievement hunting, and created some wacky empires. But after my recent umpteenth attempt at getting into the micro management hell this once fun game has become I've decided to permanently uninstall it. The direction this game has taken over the years in terms of development is moving it further and further away from what we initial players wanted. In the initial 1.0-1.9 versions you had the freedom to approach the game however you pleased, with multiple forms of space travel and empire design and a more combat oriented game. Now the game has become an economic simulator where the real enemy is your lack of resources and every game follows the same path of fortifying choke points and microing your economy to get enough alloy to afford ships. It was a great game once and while the newer DLC is great and interesting the base game itself isn't worth the cost.
